term: fixed source-constraint omission and strictness graphs
definition: fork has three nodes a,b,c with exactly a→c and b→c; a,b are distinct sources. isolated has two Bool nodes and no edges. chain has all Int nodes with edge y x iff y=x+1; integer labels index causal nodes, not temporal instants. empty has carrier Empty and no edges. OmissionControls certifies the fork is connected, well-founded and acyclic but not left-unique; isolated is left-unique and well-founded but disconnected with two sources; chain is connected, left-unique and at-most-one-source but not well-founded and has no source; Empty is connected, left-unique, well-founded and at-most-one-source but unpopulated and source-free. diamond has nodes root,left,right,tip, with root→left, root→right, left→tip, right→tip. ConfluenceStrictnessControl certifies its upstream confluence, weak connectivity, WF, failure of immediate predecessor uniqueness, and one source with paths from all nodes.
note: Explicit mathematical interpretations only, not claims that causal or metaphysical possibilities are realized. Empty connectivity uses the universal zigzag convention rather than a nonempty connected-space convention. The fixed diamond proves the sufficient left-unique restriction can be strictly weakened to upstream confluence.
